title: Urodynamic testing
what: A machine measures how your bladder fills and empties. For this, a thin catheter with a sensor is placed in the bladder.
why: For urine leaks, frequent urges, a weak stream, and before bladder or prostate surgery.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes; you usually get the findings the same day
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially for the bladder. Your doctor will decide if you need a break
If you have pain or burning when peeing right now

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: You are often asked to record for 2 to 3 days when and how much you drink and pee. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Urine test
prepare.text: A recent urine test is often needed to rule out infection.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Come with a full bladder. At the start, you will be asked to pee into a special device.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. If your doctor says to pause, they will tell you for how long.

steps: You pee into a special toilet that measures your stream
You lie down or sit in a chair
A thin catheter with a sensor goes into the bladder, and another into the rectum
The bladder is slowly filled with sterile fluid
You tell the doctor when you feel the urge to pee
At the end, you pee while the machine records the pressure
feel: An unpleasant feeling as the catheters go in
A strong urge at the end of filling. That is expected
It may feel awkward. Staff are used to it
after: Drink more water that day, unless your doctor says otherwise
Mild burning when peeing for 1 to 2 days can happen
Your doctor will discuss the results with you at your visit
red_flags: Blood in your urine for more than a day

faq.a: Usually not. The catheters are thin. It may be unpleasant and awkward, but not for long.

faq.q: What if I leak during the test?
faq.a: That is normal and even useful for the test. Staff are ready for it.

reminders.text: Urodynamic test tomorrow. Bring your bladder diary and come with a full bladder.
